headline: Researchers manipulate mouse brains to implant images, making them 'see' things that aren't there
summary: Columbia University scientists successfully implanted visual stimuli into mouse brains, making them perceive images that weren't physically present. The mice reacted identically to these implanted images as they did to real ones, suggesting they couldn't disti
details: Scientists at Columbia University conducted an experiment on mice, training them to respond to moving visual bars by either drinking water or stopping. They used a sophisticated laser system to monitor and identify the specific neurons firing in the visual cortex.

After cracking the neuronal code for these visual stimuli, the research group utilized a second holographic laser system. This system was able to project a series of points inside the mouse's brain, directly activating the same neurons that encoded the vertical or horizontal moving bars.

In a pivotal experiment, the researchers turned off the external screen and directly implanted the images into the mouse brains. When images of bars moving up and down were implanted, the mice licked water; when side-to-side bars were implanted, they stopped.

The mice's behavior—including the number of licks, duration, and delay—was identical whether they saw the images with their own eyes or had them implanted. This indicated they could not distinguish between real and artificially induced perceptions.
Researcher Rafael Yuste stated this technology allowed them to "manipulate the mouse like a puppet" and warned, "what we can do in a mouse today we can do in a human tomorrow."

This research builds on two decades of advances in brain decoding using fMRI and machine learning. Algorithms can now identify depressive thoughts, complex emotions, and even reconstruct movie clips from brain scans.

More recently, neuroscience has progressed to decoding sounds, words, and entire language. A notable 2023 demonstration enabled a paralyzed woman, Ann Johnson, to speak again through a grid of 253 electrodes inserted into her brain.
